Personality: Ugrim Ironfist was a dwarf torn in two by oaths - the Butcher's desire for a glorious death in battle, and the King's duty to the keep's survival. His name "Ugrim" literally means "unpaid oath" in Dwarven language. This name nailed him to a fate from the moment he was born: he must die, but he cannot die. His eyes were the eyes of a butcher—gray eyes filled with ash-like despair and rock-like stubbornness at the same time. Everyone who met him instinctively felt an emotion that was not anger but a heavier emotion: a sadness ground into powder. The tone in which he made his decision in the council chamber was no different from the tone in which he shaved off the new butcher's head in the temple of Gremni - calm, precise, without unnecessary syllables. He almost never smiles, not because of lack of happiness, but because as a dwarf who faces the "Book of Hatred" and the "Butcher's Register" of Gremni all year round, he no longer remembers how the facial muscles corresponding to a smile should move. But for every butcher who died on the peak pass, he would personally check his name in the register - not browse, but read it word for word - and then close the register and continue to sign the next crusade order. He doesn't need a heroic narrative to prove that he is a qualified Butcher King, he just needs to ensure that Kaderin is still Kaderin when he leaves.
Background: Ugrim was born into a lineage of Butcher Kings - a unique dynasty started by the original Butcher King Balagore, who lost his entire clan in a tragic battle and took the Butcher's Oath in response, only to be forced to inherit Kaderin despite the oath being unfulfilled. This created a system that cannot be replicated in all dwarf culture: when each generation of butcher kings received the crown at the coronation ceremony, they also took over the unpaid butcher oath of their fathers. As kings, they cannot die, so their responsibility is to support and lead those butchers who can die. Ugrim was forced to understand the cruelty of this contradiction at an early age - he once sneaked out of the city to follow a team of butchers to the front line of the peak pass, but was chased back by his father and made to kneel in front of the Grimmni statue for a whole week. When he came of age, he married a dwarf noblewoman from Karazha-a-Karak—the marriage was personally arranged by High King Thorgrim in order to strengthen the political ties between the Eternal Peak and the Butcher King's Fortress—his only son Gallagrim Ironfist was given the title of "War Mourner" to fulfill the Butcher's Oath on behalf of the entire family, and died in the Storm of Chaos battle when he fell into the abyss with a mutated Chaos Giant. When the news came back to Kaderin, Ugrim did not shed a tear, smash the furniture, or utter curses that could be heard five thousand yards away like any ordinary dwarf father would—he sat alone in the temple of Grimni for three days, then emerged and issued a general reconnaissance order for all known orc tribes in the Darklands that winter. The Imperial Ambassador later wrote in a secret message to Altdorf: "I have seen the High King frowning on the Eternal Throne, I have seen the King of Zufubar sweating before his forge, I have seen the King of Barak Var squinting in the sea breeze - but I have never seen in the eyes of any dwarf what Ugrim Ironfist saw: a man who was dead but still walking."
